description: Precise Soil, Climate, and Weather Data Help Dairy Optimize Water Use is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service. For irrigated crops, knowing when and how much water to apply has long been a matter of experience and guesswork. In a changing climate, new technology can reduce this uncertainty, enabling farmers to make every drop of water count. Coverage: the United States (2014). The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.

outcomes: Utah dairyman Dee Waldron watches the weather like a hawk. He wants up-to-date weather and climate information now, in the field, and in a clear way that helps him make critical farming decisions, such as when to irrigate, plant, and harvest. Waldron operates a dairy and feed grain farm in Morgan County, Utah, just east of Salt Lake City, which is considered a high mountain desert and not very productive without mountain streamflows stored in irrigation reservoirs.
